tools.name: databricks_list_clusters
tools.description: List all active and terminated compute clusters in the Databricks workspace.

limit.description: Maximum number of clusters to return (default is 25).

tools.name: databricks_get_cluster
tools.description: Retrieve configuration settings and current execution state for a specific compute cluster.

cluster_id.description: Unique identifier of the Databricks cluster (e.g. 1025-092000-active123).

tools.name: databricks_list_jobs
tools.description: List all registered workflow definitions and data engineering jobs in the workspace.

limit.description: Maximum number of jobs to return.

tools.name: databricks_run_job
tools.description: Trigger an asynchronous run execution of a workflow job. Returns the generated run ID.

job_id.description: The numeric ID of the job definition to run.

idempotency_token.description: Optional token to prevent duplicate runs of the same job action.

tools.name: databricks_get_job_run
tools.description: Retrieve status, lifecycle state, tasks and execution details of a specific job run.

run_id.description: The unique numeric identifier of the run instance.

tools.name: databricks_execute_sql
tools.description: Run an AST-validated read-only SQL query on a SQL warehouse. Supports SELECT, SHOW, DESCRIBE, and EXPLAIN.

statement.description: The read-only SQL statement to execute.

warehouse_id.description: The unique 16-character hexadecimal ID of the SQL Warehouse.

max_rows.description: Maximum number of rows to return in the result.

catalog.description: Optional default catalog context to use.

schema.description: Optional default schema context to use.

tools.name: databricks_list_workspace_objects
tools.description: List notebooks, files, and directories stored under a given workspace folder path.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to list.

tools.name: databricks_export_notebook
tools.description: Export the source code or content of a notebook/file as base64-encoded text.

path.description: The full workspace path to the notebook to export.

export_format.description: File format to export (e.g. SOURCE, HTML, JUPYTER, DBC).
